summary: Redwood AE and SE gave a Console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and token-level cost breakdowns. Customer (Solaris Health) asked about per-route filtering, burst/batching controls, KV/prefix caching impact, and security compliance (SOC 2, SSO/SAML). topics: Console demo, per-route dashboards, token cost breakdown, batching & caching impact, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, security (SOC2, SSO), pilot benchmarks, next steps
transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-09-30 14:30 UTC - Duration 46m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Morris (Solaris Health), Samir Khan (Solaris Eng), Priya Nair (CTO)
Link: (demo deck) https://redwood-demo/s/console-usage-2026-09-30

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Ravi my SE is with me, we'll do a quick 30 minute console walkthrough focused on usage analytics and per-route cost breakdowns, then leave time for Q&A.
[00:18] Priya Nair: Thanks, Maya. We only have about 45 minutes, so appreciate the focused demo. Our infra lead Samir and head of data Elena are on.
[00:30] Ravi Patel: Great, quick agenda - show per-route dashboards, token-level cost visibility, call out batching/caching levers in Optimize, then talk about pilots and security.
[00:45] Dr. Elena Morris: Awesome, interested in the token-level breakdown - we need to understand cost by endpoint and by team.

[02:15] Ravi Patel: Ok I'm sharing my screen - here's the Console home, top-line usage metrics. You can see QPS and cost over time, and we group by route. Let me click into a route - this is "medical-summarize-v1" route you might map to a clinician summary path.
[02:48] Ravi Patel: Notice the route dashboard shows tokens in, tokens out, avg latency, errors, and importantly cost per 1k tokens. We also surface percent of cost attributable to embeddings vs generative tokens.
[03:20] Samir Khan: Is the per-route mapping manual or can it map automatically from path patterns?
[03:30] Maya Chen: You can tag routes programmatically via SDKs or the API, and also set matching rules for path patterns. We usually do a quick naming convention integration.

[04:10] Ravi Patel: Here's a filter: we can slice by customer-team tag, environment (prod/staging), or by model family. See this example where we compare two routes side-by-side for last 7 days.
[04:45] Ravi Patel: The interesting part - cost breakdown. Tokens are split into prompt tokens, completion tokens, and embedding units. The Console projects monthly spend based on current run rate and shows estimated savings if you enable batching/caching or switch to a quantized variant.

[06:05] Dr. Elena Morris: When you say batching, is that automatic at the runtime layer? We tried manual batching in our infra but it adds complexity.
[06:18] Ravi Patel: Good question. Redwood's serving runtime does continuous batching where appropriate. In the Console Optimize tab we show recommended batching window and expected cost/latency tradeoff. For example, enabling 50ms micro-batching for your summary route could save ~23% on token cost with negligible P50 latency impact, based on similar workloads.
[07:00] Priya Nair: Can we see where KV/prefix caching helps? Our flows reuse conversation prefixes a lot.
[07:12] Ravi Patel: Yes, on the route dashboard we simulate cache hit rates. Here see a chart - with a 70% KV cache hit rate your effective per-token generation drops significantly. We also show the delta in calls to the model (fewer decoded tokens) and the downstream cost reduction.

[08:05] Samir Khan: How accurate are these projections? We run enterprise budgets and need predictability.
[08:14] Maya Chen: Projections are based on historical usage patterns from your route and model profile. We include conservative and aggressive scenarios. For pilots we run a short benchmark that uses your prompt set which gives much tighter estimates - that's what we recommend for budgeting.

[09:40] Ravi Patel: Switching to Alerts and Anomalies - Console can create cost alerts per-route (absolute and % change) and tie them back to tokens/spikes. We also expose trace links so you can see the exact requests that caused the spike.
[10:05] Dr. Elena Morris: Do those traces contain PHI? We need to ensure they don't store PII/PHI in logs.
[10:13] Maya Chen: By default traces are metadata-only; raw payloads are redacted for hosted customers, and for Private deployments you control retention and storage. We support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest, and audit logging for access.

[11:30] Ravi Patel: Now I'll demo the Rate & Routing tab - you can set policies per-route: prefer-hosted, prefer-dedicated, region-priority, and fallback model variants. This lets you serve low-latency routes on Dedicated pools and fall back to hosted when capacity is reached.
[12:05] Priya Nair: We have regulatory regional constraints, can we pin a route to a specific region?
[12:12] Ravi Patel: Yes, you can pin by region or by instance group. The Console shows the routing map and estimates latency by region.

[13:00] Ravi Patel: Quick note on model variants and quantization - the Console will recommend a quantized variant for cost reduction and show expected quality delta based on your eval suite; we also provide per-route eval metrics if you've run evals tied to the route.
[13:40] Samir Khan: For our clinical summarization we can't compromise quality. How do you measure regressions?
[13:48] Maya Chen: We recommend creating a small eval prompt set with key golden examples. Redwood Optimize runs A/B comparisons and surfaces regression alerts if output quality drops beyond thresholds. We can help design the eval.

[15:20] Ravi Patel: Now walking through a concrete cost example - here's a 30-day view for two routes. Route A (summaries) consumed 1.2M tokens and cost $3,600; Route B (triage chat) consumed 4.5M tokens and cost $6,700. If you enable KV cache on Route A and switch Route B to a 4-bit quantized variant for non-critical endpoints, projected monthly cost drops ~28%.
[15:58] Dr. Elena Morris: That 4-bit quantized variant - do you support that on Dedicated only?
[16:05] Ravi Patel: We support quantized variants across deployments but Dedicated gives you better deterministic throughput and can host custom quantized models if needed. Hosted also has quantized options for many open models.

[17:30] Priya Nair: On data residency and security, we need SOC 2 + SSO/SAML and support for customer-managed KMS.
[17:40] Maya Chen: We are SOC 2 Type II, support SSO/SAML, role-based access control (RBAC), and customer KMS via our Private offering. We'll send the SOC2 report and architecture doc after the call.

[19:05] Ravi Patel: Quick demo of the Cost Explorer - you can break down costs by model, route, team, or tag. Exportable CSVs for finance. Also a forecast mode to see month-end projection based on smoothing algorithms.
[19:40] Samir Khan: Can we set hard caps per-route? Not just alerts.
[19:46] Ravi Patel: Yes, you can enforce budget caps per-route with blocking or throttling policies; Console will surface errors back to callers. For sensitive flows we recommend soft alerts first then hard caps during pilot.

[21:10] Dr. Elena Morris: For the pilot, can you run with our prompt set and simulate our traffic pattern including bursts?
[21:20] Ravi Patel: Absolutely. We usually run a 7-14 day benchmark that replays your prompts and QPS pattern on a dedicated test pool and report token-level cost, latency distributions, and recommended config (batch size, cache TTL, model variant).

[22:00] Priya Nair: Do you provide sample infra IaC to wire up the routing and SSO for Private?
[22:06] Maya Chen: Yes, we have Terraform modules and deployment guides for VPC/private deployments. We'll share those links.

[23:00] Ravi Patel: A note on billing granularity - we bill tokens and embeddings separately; Console reconciles with your invoice and shows per-route chargebacks so you can map cost back to internal teams.

[24:15] Samir Khan: Any gotchas with long-running KV caches and memory?
[24:22] Ravi Patel: We give memory and TTL controls per-route and an estimate of the KV cache working set. For very large KV requirements you can bring your own store and we support connectors.

[26:00] Ravi Patel: Ok I'll flip to a live pilot results example from another healthcare customer (anonymized) - shows similar summary routes, 3 week pilot, 20% cost reduction via caching + micro-batching. Note: numbers vary with prompt complexity.
[26:35] Dr. Elena Morris: Sounds promising. Any SLA for Dedicated latency?
[26:42] Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency tiers; we'll include latency SLO options in the pricing packet.

[28:10] Priya Nair: For compliance, do you provide SIEM integration?
[28:18] Maya Chen: Yes we integrate with common SIEMs and outbound log sinks, plus audit logs you can pull into your SIEM.

[29:00] Ravi Patel: Back to the Console, here's the audit log viewer and per-token privacy redaction note. And the rollout control where you can do canary/beta for a route.

[30:15] Samir Khan: If we start with hosted pilot and then move to Dedicated, how much friction is there?
[30:24] Maya Chen: Minimal - routing policies let you migrate routes; console persists audit, dashboards, and route configs. We help with migration planning.

[31:40] Dr. Elena Morris: Ok are there any additional costs for the Optimize recommendations?
[31:46] Maya Chen: Optimize is included with enterprise tiers; advanced recommendations and on-call SE support are add-ons. We'll clarify in the pricing doc.

[33:05] Ravi Patel: Questions from our side - what success metrics will you use for the pilot?
[33:12] Dr. Elena Morris: Cost per 1k tokens by route, P95 latency under 350ms for summaries, no quality regressions on 10 gold examples.
[33:25] Priya Nair: And timeline - decision by end of October ideally.

[34:00] Maya Chen: Great, recap of next steps - we'll send pricing and SOC2 docs, Ravi will draft pilot plan and we schedule benchmark week of Oct 11, and Elena will share prompt sets.

[34:20] Samir Khan: One last question: do you support enterprise chargeback exports?
[34:28] Ravi Patel: Yes exports and API access for cost data.

[35:00] Priya Nair: Thanks, that was very thorough.

[35:10] Maya Chen: Thank you all - we'll follow up with the items.

[35:20] Dr. Elena Morris: Thanks, talk soon.

End of call.

Notes: Some transcription artifacts - Speaker labels may flip; occasional word errors (e.g., KV cache transcribed as KV cash). Demo links and screenshots referenced in chat.

Recap / Agreed next steps:
- Maya to share tailored pricing and per-route cost model + SOC2 and architecture docs
- Ravi to prepare pilot benchmark plan (7-14 days) and estimate resources
- Solaris to share prompt sets and QPS targets
- Schedule pilot week of 2026-10-11
